court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Civil Judge, Junior Division, Ausa in Regular Civil Suit No.292 of 2000
case_name: Digambar Namdeo Munjal And Ors vs Kashibai Digambar Munjal And Ors

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Digambar s/o. Namdeo Munjal and others (defendants)
parties.respondent_defendant: Kashibai w/o. Digambar Munjal (died) and others (plaintiffs)

facts_of_case: Plaintiffs filed suit for partition and separate possession of their share in land. Defendant No.1 illegally transferred suit lands to defendant Nos.2 and 3. Plaintiffs contended that suit lands are ancestral joint family properties.

legal_principles.principle: The appellate Court must consider what are the points involved in the matter and formulate the points for determination before delivering its decision.
legal_principles.held: When the appellate Court has reversed the judgment of the trial Court, it was absolutely necessary for the first appellate Court to consider what were the points involved in the matter and accordingly formulate the points for determination and then deal with those points with regard to the materials on record.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order 41, Rule 31

legal_principles.principle: The appellate Court must deal with the points formulated for determination with regard to the materials on record.
legal_principles.held: Then deal with those points with regard to the materials on record.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order 41, Rule 31

legal_principles.principle: An illegitimate child will get a share in the self-acquired property of his/her parents, but not in the ancestral property.
legal_principles.held: Illegitimate child (will) get share in the self acquired property of his/her parents and not in the ancestral property.

outcome.final_order: The appellants' appeal against dismissal of their Regular Civil Appeal No.283 of 2012 was allowed.
